nodes.bodyText: note: `UnreadPosts` is per post now, so a map's new state isn't invented any more.
praise: Yes, and that's what lets the finder mark new replies.
nitpick (non-blocking): `card_gap` and `card_margin` are both 8; one constant would do.
They drift apart at Discuss widths, so I kept both.
praise: Fair, and the names say why.
question: Who still calls `set_feed()` once Discuss has its own list?
issue (blocking): `set_current_thread()` keeps a reply's id when no card holds it, so `Current` can name nothing.
question: Should it clear `Current` instead, or keep the last card?
praise: Good catch, this explains the lost highlight after a refresh.
Clear it. I'll push the fix with a test.
question: Should this traversal keep the selected node when the card list is rebuilt?
It does: `Current` holds an id, not a row, so a rebuild can't move it.
Unless the card that held the id is gone after the rebuild.
question: What about a parent that arrives after its child, on the next page?
question: Then what does `Current` name? Nothing, until the next click?
That's the bug tbutler filed on line 656.
Right. I'll fall back to the nearest card in file order.
thought: Nearest by line, or by position in the list?
The child is promoted to a root until its parent lands.
And when it lands, does the selection jump?
suggestion (non-blocking, if-minor): Look the id up in an index instead of walking every card's posts.
The index would need rebuilding on every refresh too.
By line. The list order changes with the scope.
praise: Line it is. That also keeps the code view still.
It shouldn't. The id is the same; only its depth changes.
It's built in `relayout()` already, so the lookup is free here.
Then the walk becomes a lookup. Worth it at 500 cards?
Measured: 0.4 ms against 0.02. Not urgent.
nitpick: Leave a comment pointing at the measurement, then.
thought (perf): Aside: `relayout()` also runs twice on a scope change. Separate card?
Agreed. Branch A's fix first, this after.
Yes, filed it. The second pass finds nothing to do.
issue (blocking): The test only loads one page, so paging is never exercised here.
todo: Adding a two-page case to the hostile fixtures.
Thanks. Ping me when it's up.
praise: Thanks for splitting it out.
suggestion: `relayout()` is 200 lines; measuring and placing could be two functions.
They share `compactMeasurements`, so splitting means passing it around.
Passing one struct is fine. The measuring half has no side effects.
thought: Then the placing half could be tested without fonts.
Which would have caught the 280 px clipping last week.
note (perf): `relayout()` runs twice on a scope change; the second pass finds nothing to do.
Splitting after this lands, on its own card.
praise: Thanks, happy with that.
Why `width - 2 * card_margin` and not the viewport's `contentsRect()`?
The viewport has no margins here, so `contentsRect()` is the same width.
nitpick (non-blocking): Then a comment saying so would stop the next person asking.
thought (perf): `std::max` here pushes every later card down one by one; does a run of close lines cost a pass each?
It's one pass over sorted cards, so linear either way.
Right, I misread the loop.
chore (non-blocking): Say in a comment that Shift+F10 and the Menu key open the same thread menu.
+1, the second half of the condition on 1512 is easy to miss.
nitpick: The cache key leaves out the label marks theme, so switching themes keeps the old heights.
suggestion (non-blocking): `apply()` moves rows one at a time; a reset would be cheaper past 500 rows.
A reset loses the selection, which is the thing this pull request keeps.
question: Once the drawer is inline only, who still calls `synchronize_map_focus()`?
The finder would, if it keeps the picked reply.
thought: Restoring by identity is what keeps the picked reply after a refresh. Worth a test that picks a deep one.
todo (if-minor): Adding it to the branching fixture.
question: Why an explicit stack and not recursion?
A hostile fixture is 10,000 deep; recursion would run out of stack.
That's `valid-deep-wide-tree`'s cousin in the hostile set.
thought: Then the comment should say depth is the reason, not taste.
It says pre-order is the point; depth isn't mentioned.
Could `Depth` be computed when placing instead of here?
suggestion: Keep it here; placing reads it for every edge.
Agreed, and name the bound on `pending`.
praise: The no-crossing property in one sentence is lovely.
nitpick (non-blocking): `order.reserve` could come first. It already does; ignore me.
Leaving it.
Rebased on main; the hostile fixtures still pass.
issue (blocking): A parent that arrives on the next page is promoted to a root and never re-parented.
The map is rebuilt when that page lands, so it re-parents then.
question: Is there a test for that?
Not yet. I'll add one with the paged fixture.
Thanks, I'll wait for it.
question: Should a focus change announce itself when the drawer moved it?
nitpick: `reveal_branch()` could share its margin with `reveal()`.
Done.
chore (non-blocking): `insert_or_move()` could log its moves under the diagnostics flag.
Done in the next push.
issue (blocking): Carry `ReplyTo`, not the root. Where does a first comment fall back?
A first comment's `ReplyTo` is empty, so it falls back to the root.
Then say so in a test.
todo: Adding one.
suggestion: Say why `ParentId` is empty here; it reads like a bug.
Agreed.
praise: The version check before advancing reads well.
issue: This guards against read state the ledger now carries; it should check the map uses it instead.
question: Rename it, or let `test_unread_nodes_are_filled_from_the_ledger_state` cover it?
Let 599 cover it and delete this one.
